name: A timed-out engine call leaves its container running
description:
Raised by Tomáš in the review of PR #84 (CZ3TDR1-735). Pre-existing and true of every engine queue, not introduced by that PR.

## The mechanism

`runEngineCli` (`packages/runner/src/engine-sandbox.ts`) runs `docker run --rm …` through execa with `timeout: engineTimeoutMs()` and `killSignal: "SIGKILL"`, and passes an optional `signal`. When either fires, execa kills the `docker run` client process, not the container. A SIGKILL cannot be proxied to the container, and the engine path sets no `--name` (`EngineSandboxSpec.containerName` exists, but only the dynamic probe passes one, in `dynamic-test.ts`) and runs no `docker kill` afterwards. So the call returns a timeout to the handler while the container keeps running — and keeps calling the provider — until the engine CLI inside it exits on its own. `--rm` removes it only then.

## What it costs

Handler-side timing is correct: the call returns at the timeout, so the job's own bookkeeping (and #84's verifier deadline) holds. What does not hold is any claim about spend or container count: a provider outage or a hung CLI leaves orphaned containers billing in the background, and the "a timed-out call costs one call's worth" reading in the comments is true of handler time, not of container lifetime. The same applies to an aborted call once `job.signal` is passed through.

## Fix (to decide)

Give every engine container a name (`containerName` already exists on the spec) and, when execa reports a timeout or an abort, `docker kill` it by that name before rethrowing. Then correct the comments that equate "the call was killed" with "the container stopped" (`reconcile-findings.ts` near `VERIFIER_RESERVE_MS`, the reconcile queue comment in `apps/worker/src/index.ts`).

**Done when:** a timed-out or aborted engine call leaves no container running, a test pins the kill on both paths, and no comment claims the timeout stops the container unless it does.
